How Much Does a 2017 Audi R8 Cost After 53,000 Miles?
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Audi pulled the plug on the R8 two years ago, but that does not make it any less exciting, as we are still looking at a German supercar with Italian influences.
That’s because it may have been assembled at the Heilbronn facility in Germany by the four-ring brand, but beneath the skin lies the same platform as the Lamborghini Huracan. The Raging Bull’s previous-generation baby supercar was dropped for good in 2024, being replaced with the Temerario, and the R8 followed in its footsteps, as the assembly ceased in 2024 as well, after a ten-year production run.
During this time, the second-generation Audi R8 was offered as a two-door coupe and a two-door convertible (Spyder) featuring rear-wheel drive on certain models, and all-wheel drive on others. All of them had a longitudinal mid-engine layout, and packed the same mill as the Huracan. And that’s a 5.2-liter naturally aspirated V10, in case you forgot, which was good for 533 horsepower (540 ps/397 kW) in the base model.
Bring the V10 Plus variant into discussion, and the output will increase to 602 hp (610 ps/449 kW), and the thrust to 413 pound-feet (560 Nm), unlike the entry-level variant that offered 398 lb-ft (540 Nm) of torque originally. The lineup also comprises the R8 V10 RWS and R8 V10 Spyder RWS, with 533 hp (540 ps/397 kW) and 398 lb-ft (540 Nm) of torque, and the Spyder body style was also offered on other flavors of the supercar.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Even the slowest version of the second-generation Audi R8 took a couple of tenths of a second below the 4-second mark to reach 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, whereas the quickest did it in a little over three seconds. The top speed varied from one version to the other and from one body style to the other, and it ranged between 197 and 205 mph (317-330 kph).
The facelifted iteration was even faster, and the R8 V10 Performance Quattro, which was offered as a Coupe and Spyder, had 612 horsepower (620 ps/456 kW) and 428 pound-feet (580 Nm) of torque to play with, dropping the sprint time to 3.1 seconds, and increasing the maximum speed to 206 mph (331 kph) for the Coupe, and 3.2 seconds and 204 mph (329 kph) for the Spyder.
Audi’s second-generation R8 was briefly joined by the e-tron , which was introduced at the 2015 Geneva Motor Show. This was a battery-electric model with 456 horsepower in total from its pair of motors, four seconds required to zip to 62 mph, and a 280-mile (450 km) range promised by the four-ring brand. Thus, the company had an electric supercar before it was cool.
Now, we have talked about the second-gen Audi R8 as a whole a bit too much, so we should finally put the spotlight on the example pictured in the gallery, which is the whole reason behind this story. It is a 2027 model year supercar, as mentioned in the title, and as you can see, it features a blue paint finish on the outside, has the usual black details, rides on black wheels that spin around the gray brake calipers, and also sports tinted windows.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago While the exterior is definitely sporty and quite exotic , the cockpit is on the gentleman side of things due to the use of brown leather upholstery on the seats, on the center console, and on parts of the door cards. The seats have diamond quilting on them, the pillars, headliner, and other parts of the interior were wrapped in black Alcantara, and we can also see some carbon fiber trim, a few metallic accents, and other bits and bobs.
This 2017 Audi R8 is said to have some 53,000 miles (85,300 km) on the clock, which makes it a high mileage supercar, though for what it’s worth, it looks very good for a blue-blooded exotic that has seen so much action over the years. There is a bit of wear on the driver’s seat outer bolsters, yet other than that, we do not see other flaws.
A 2017 model year Audi R8 usually ranges between $120,000 and upward of $170,000 for the V10 Plus Coupe, and if you want to spruce up your life with something like this, then you should not forget that its high maintenance could easily bankrupt you. After all, we are still talking about a supercar, and one that shares its DNA with a defunct Lambo.
But how much do you think one must cough out if they want to write their name on the dotted line in the papers of the pictured Audi R8? That would be $159,995, which was the asking price at the time of writing. We found this R8 on social media advertised by @motorcarsofchicago, and it is up to you to decide whether or not it’s worth that kind of money.
